question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined phrase.

In the absence of government rule, riots have broken out all over the country and everything is in a state of complete chaos.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Anarchy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "in the absence of government rule" with "riots" and "complete chaos" describes a state of lawlessness and disorder. The word that captures this is "anarchy" — a situation of disorder due to the absence of authority or government. (अराजकता)

◦ Correct: In the absence of government rule, everything descends into anarchy.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Oligarchy" = rule by a small privileged group.

• Option 3 "Dictatorship" = rule by a single all-powerful person.

• Option 4 "Monarchy" = rule by a king or queen.

NOTE

• Related terms: anarchy (no government/order), democracy (rule by the people), aristocracy (rule by the nobility), theocracy (rule by religious authority), plutocracy (rule by the wealthy).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The detail given by the instructor was the ______ one.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. most updated.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The definite article "the" before the blank and the singular noun "one" signal the superlative degree, so "the most updated one" is correct. "Updated" also works as a past-participle adjective describing "detail". (सबसे नवीनतम)

◦ Correct: The detail given by the instructor was the most updated one.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "more updation" — "updation" is non-standard and "more" (comparative) does not fit "the ... one".

• Option 3 "updating" and Option 4 "updates" are grammatically wrong here (a form of "one" needs an adjective).

NOTE

• With a long adjective, the superlative is formed with "the most" (the most updated / the most modern), while the comparative uses "more ... than".

question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.

You can do your work well within the stipulated time and be more productive if you learn to keep video games at the length of your arm.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. at arm’s length.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "at arm’s length" means to keep someone/something at a distance; to avoid becoming too involved. It fits the sense of keeping video games away/at a distance. (दूरी बनाए रखना)

◦ Correct: ... if you learn to keep video games at arm’s length.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 2 and 3 distort the fixed idiom ("at arm of his length", "at arm’s weight", "at arm of your length") and are not standard English.

NOTE

• Note the possessive form "arm’s" (singular possessive). Similar distance idioms: "keep at bay", "give a wide berth", "steer clear of".

question:
Select the most appropriate homophone to fill in the blank.

Looking up, she realised she had swum __________ than she’d thought.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. farther.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Farther" is the comparative of "far" used for physical/measurable distance. As "swum" refers to an actual distance covered in water, "farther than" is correct. (अधिक दूर)

◦ Correct: ... she had swum farther than she’d thought.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2 "furthest" and 3 "farthest" are superlatives and cannot be used with "than".

• Option 4 "further" is generally used for abstract/figurative extent (e.g., "further information", "further discussion"), so "farther" is the better fit for literal distance.

NOTE

• Farther/farthest → physical distance; further/furthest → additional/abstract degree. With "than" a comparative (farther/further) is required, not a superlative.

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

The recommendations of the committee / regarding changes in the eligibility criteria / was not accept.
option_2: regarding changes in the eligibility criteria
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. was not accept.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject "recommendations" is plural, so the verb must be plural — "were", not "was". Also, after "were not", the past participle "accepted" is needed (passive voice), not the base verb "accept". So the segment should be "were not accepted".

◦ Correct: The recommendations of the committee regarding changes in the eligibility criteria were not accepted.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "The recommendations of the committee" and "regarding changes in the eligibility criteria" are grammatically correct.

• The error is one of both subject–verb agreement and passive-voice form.

NOTE

• Passive voice = be-verb + past participle (V3): "were accepted", "was rejected". Ensure the be-verb agrees with the real subject (recommendations → were).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

He sings good / among all the / contestants in / the singing competition.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. He sings good.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Sings" is a verb and must be modified by an adverb, not the adjective "good". The correct adverb is "well". So it should be "He sings well".

◦ Correct: He sings well among all the contestants in the singing competition.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "among all the", "contestants in" and "the singing competition" are all correct.

• "Good" describes a noun (a good singer); "well" describes how an action is done (sings well).

NOTE

• Common adjective/adverb confusions: good/well, bad/badly, quick/quickly. Verbs of action take adverbs (runs fast, works hard, sings well).

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. paralel.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Paralel" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "parallel" (having two l’s), meaning side by side and always the same distance apart; comparable. (समानांतर)

◦ Spelling key: PAR + AL + LEL — note the double "l".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "humorous" (funny), "achieve" (to accomplish) and "familiar" (well known) are all correctly spelt.

• Remember "achieve" follows the rule "i before e except after c".

NOTE

• Frequently misspelt: parallel, necessary, occurrence, embarrass, millennium — watch the double letters carefully.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Consciencious.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Consciencious" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "conscientious", meaning careful, thorough and taking one’s duties seriously. (कर्तव्यनिष्ठ)

◦ Spelling key: CON + SCIEN + TIOUS.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Unanimous" (in complete agreement), "Millennium" (a period of 1000 years) and "Inconvenience" (trouble/difficulty) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Related words: conscience (sense of right and wrong — noun), conscientious (dutiful — adjective), conscious (aware). Do not confuse conscience/conscious.

question: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
option_1: A myriad of possibilities unfolds when the artist embarks on the journey of creative experimentation.
option_2: A myriad of possibilities unfolds when an artist embarks on a journey of creative experimentation.
option_3: The myriad of possibilities unfolds when the artist embarks on a journey of creative experimentation.
option_4: The myriad of possibilities unfolds when an artist embarks on the journey of creative experimentation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. A myriad of possibilities unfolds when an artist embarks on a journey of creative experimentation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct usage is "a myriad of" (with the indefinite article "a"), and general statements use the indefinite article — "an artist", "a journey" — because no specific artist or journey is meant.

◦ Correct: A myriad of possibilities unfolds when an artist embarks on a journey of creative experimentation.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Options 3 and 4 wrongly use "The myriad" and specific "the" for general nouns.

• Option 1 uses "the artist" and "the journey", implying particular ones, which does not suit a general statement.

NOTE

• "Myriad" can be used as "a myriad of + plural noun" or simply "myriad + plural noun" (myriad possibilities). Use "a/an" for non-specific singular countable nouns in general statements.

question:
Select the word that has the same meaning (SYNONYM) as the underlined word in the given sentence.

The prisoners were living in appalling conditions.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. shocking.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Appalling" means causing horror or dismay; shockingly bad; dreadful. Its closest synonym is "shocking". (भयावह / अत्यंत बुरा)

◦ Example: The refugees were living in appalling/shocking conditions.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "daring" (bold/courageous), Option 2 "ingenuous" (innocent/naive) and Option 3 "risky" (dangerous) do not match.

NOTE

• Synonyms of appalling: shocking, horrifying, dreadful, atrocious, terrible. Antonyms: pleasant, wonderful, admirable.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

One who brings a legal action against someone in court.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Plaintiff.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "plaintiff" is a person who brings a case/legal action against another in a court of law. (वादी / मुद्दई)

◦ Example: The plaintiff filed a suit against the company for breach of contract.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Sanctimonious" (making a show of being morally superior) is an adjective, not a person.

• Option 2 "Numismatic" relates to the study/collection of coins.

• Option 3 "Pragmatist" (a practical, realistic person) does not fit.

NOTE

• Legal one-word substitutes: plaintiff (one who sues), defendant (one who is sued), plaintiff vs. accused, witness (one who gives evidence), jury (a group deciding a verdict).

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Absense.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Absense" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "absence" (with a "c"), meaning the state of being away/not present. (अनुपस्थिति)

◦ Spelling key: AB + SENCE → absence.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Abstract" (not concrete), "Abscess" (a swollen area containing pus) and "Abstinent" (refraining from something) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Related: absent (adjective), absence (noun), absentee (one who is absent). Note "absence" ends in "-ence", not "-ense".

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’.

There have been numerous attempts made by the citizens to restore parity.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Most numerous.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the official answer key, the underlined segment "numerous" is to be substituted with the superlative form "most numerous", emphasising that the attempts made by the citizens were the greatest in number.

◦ Substituted: There have been most numerous attempts made by the citizens to restore parity.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "More numerous" is a comparative and would need a "than" clause for a valid comparison.

• Option 4 "Quite numerous" merely softens the sense and was not the intended key.

NOTE

• Degrees of "numerous": numerous (positive) – more numerous (comparative, with "than") – most numerous (superlative). Always record the printed Correct Answer as the official key.

question:
Select the word that is opposite in meaning (ANTONYM) to the highlighted word in the given sentence.

We enjoyed the gentle breeze that was blowing.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. violent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Gentle" means mild, soft and calm. Its antonym is "violent", meaning forceful, fierce and intense. (कोमल का विलोम — प्रचंड / हिंसक)

◦ Example: The gentle breeze soon became a violent storm.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 4 "soft" is a synonym of gentle.

• Option 2 "garnished" (decorated) and Option 3 "modest" (humble) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of gentle: mild, soft, tender, calm. Antonyms: violent, harsh, rough, fierce.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Siva is a hard worker. He works ___________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. hard.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Here "hard" is an adverb meaning with great effort. Since Siva is a "hard worker", he "works hard". (कठिन परिश्रम से)

◦ Correct: Siva is a hard worker. He works hard.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "hardly" is a different word meaning "scarcely / almost not", which would reverse the meaning (he hardly works = he barely works).

• Option 1 "bad" and Option 2 "scarcely" do not fit.

NOTE

• "Hard" and "hardly" are not related in meaning: "He works hard" (with effort) vs "He hardly works" (almost not at all). "Hard" is both an adjective and an adverb.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.

I could _____ the reason for being _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. find; fined.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The first blank needs a verb meaning "to discover" → "find". The second blank needs a word meaning "made to pay a penalty" → "fined". (कारण ढूँढ़ना; जुर्माना लगाया जाना)

◦ Correct: I could find the reason for being fined.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• These are homophones/near-homophones: find (discover) vs fined (penalised); bard (a poet) vs barred (blocked/prohibited).

• Options 1, 2 and 4 place these words where they make no sense.

NOTE

• Homophone sets to remember: find/fined, bard/barred, board/bored, plain/plane. Meaning decides the choice, not just sound.

question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.

Siliguri has joined the nation to celebrate the golden jubilee of the first conquest of Mount Everest by an Indian.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. No improvement required.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "Siliguri has joined the nation to celebrate the golden jubilee ..." is already grammatically correct. The present perfect "has joined" + the infinitive of purpose "to celebrate" is proper.

◦ Correct (unchanged): Siliguri has joined the nation to celebrate the golden jubilee of the first conquest of Mount Everest by an Indian.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "joins the celebratory nation" changes the tense and meaning.

• Option 2 "joining the nation celebrate" is grammatically broken.

• Option 4 "joined the national celebration" alters the intended structure.

NOTE

• "To + verb" (infinitive of purpose) explains why an action is done: "joined ... to celebrate", "went ... to study". No change is needed when the original is already correct.

question: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
option_1: Our Principal is a great teacher and administrator.
option_2: Our Principal is a great teacher and a great administrator.
option_3: Our Principal is a great teacher and an administrator.
option_4: Our Principal is great teacher and administrator.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Our Principal is a great teacher and administrator.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When one person performs two roles, the article "a/an" is used only once before the first noun, and the adjective "great" applies to both: "a great teacher and administrator" (one and the same person).

◦ Correct: Our Principal is a great teacher and administrator.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "a great teacher and a great administrator" would suggest they may be two different persons (article repeated).

• Option 3 mixes articles incorrectly; Option 4 omits the necessary article "a".

NOTE

• Rule: one article for one person/thing in two capacities (a poet and philosopher = same person); repeat the article for two separate persons/things (a poet and a philosopher = two people).

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to substitute the underlined word segment in the given sentence.

If the two families could forget their past quarrels forever, both could benefit immensely.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. bury the hatchet.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "bury the hatchet" means to end a quarrel and make peace; to forget past disputes. It fits "forget their past quarrels forever". (पुराना झगड़ा भुलाकर सुलह कर लेना)

◦ Correct: If the two families could bury the hatchet, both could benefit immensely.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "cut to the quick" = to hurt someone's feelings deeply.

• Option 2 "catch a tartar" = to deal with someone more powerful than expected.

• Option 3 "do a good turn" = to do a kind/helpful act.

NOTE

• Similar peace idioms: "bury the hatchet", "make up", "let bygones be bygones", "mend fences".

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Presumably
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Unlikely.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Presumably" means very probably; as may reasonably be assumed/likely. Its antonym is "unlikely" (not probable). (संभवतः का विलोम — असंभावित)

◦ Example: He will presumably (likely) come — as opposed to it being unlikely.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Certainly" (definitely) is closer to a synonym in the sense of assurance.

• Options 2 "Liberally" and 4 "Successfully" are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of presumably: probably, likely, seemingly, apparently. Antonyms: unlikely, improbably, doubtfully.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The habit of reading is highly advantageous to us intellectually, emotionally and spiritually. As one gets into the habit of reading, one gets mental (1)________. It helps us acquire (2)________ and attain intellectual (3)_________. Reading takes away our (4)_________. Reading can bring (5)__________ in our sorrowful times and guide us in our duties.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. satisfaction.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage praises reading as beneficial, so "one gets mental satisfaction" (a feeling of contentment/fulfilment) fits the positive tone. (मानसिक संतुष्टि)

◦ Correct: As one gets into the habit of reading, one gets mental satisfaction.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "coverage" and Option 2 "success" do not collocate naturally with "mental" here.

• Option 4 "exhaustion" (tiredness) has a negative sense that contradicts the passage.

NOTE

• Collocations with "mental": mental satisfaction, mental peace, mental strength, mental health. Choose the word that matches the overall positive tone of the passage.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The habit of reading is highly advantageous to us intellectually, emotionally and spiritually. As one gets into the habit of reading, one gets mental (1)________. It helps us acquire (2)________ and attain intellectual (3)_________. Reading takes away our (4)_________. Reading can bring (5)__________ in our sorrowful times and guide us in our duties.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. knowledge.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Reading "helps us acquire knowledge" — information, facts and understanding — which links naturally to the next idea of intellectual growth. (ज्ञान अर्जित करना)

◦ Correct: It helps us acquire knowledge and attain intellectual expansion.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "readiness", Option 2 "employment" and Option 4 "strategies" do not fit the idea of what reading primarily gives us.

• "Acquire knowledge" is a very common and natural collocation.

NOTE

• Common collocations: acquire knowledge, gain experience, develop skills. The intellectual theme of the passage points to "knowledge".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The habit of reading is highly advantageous to us intellectually, emotionally and spiritually. As one gets into the habit of reading, one gets mental (1)________. It helps us acquire (2)________ and attain intellectual (3)_________. Reading takes away our (4)_________. Reading can bring (5)__________ in our sorrowful times and guide us in our duties.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. expansion.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Reading helps us "attain intellectual expansion" — a broadening/growth of the mind and understanding. This matches the theme of intellectual benefit. (बौद्धिक विस्तार)

◦ Correct: It helps us acquire knowledge and attain intellectual expansion.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "stagnation" (no growth) and Option 3 "compression" (reduction) are the opposite of growth.

• Option 1 "creation" does not collocate well with "intellectual".

NOTE

• "Intellectual expansion/growth/development" all convey the broadening of the mind. Pick the positive, growth-oriented word to match the passage.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The habit of reading is highly advantageous to us intellectually, emotionally and spiritually. As one gets into the habit of reading, one gets mental (1)________. It helps us acquire (2)________ and attain intellectual (3)_________. Reading takes away our (4)_________. Reading can bring (5)__________ in our sorrowful times and guide us in our duties.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. boredom.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Reading takes away our boredom" — it removes dullness and keeps the mind engaged. This is a well-known benefit of reading. (ऊब / नीरसता दूर करना)

◦ Correct: Reading takes away our boredom.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "vigour" (energy) is positive — reading would not "take away" something good.

• Options 1 "time" and 4 "concern" do not fit as well as "boredom" in this positive context.

NOTE

• "Take away boredom" means to relieve/remove dullness. Choose the negative feeling that reading is said to remove.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The habit of reading is highly advantageous to us intellectually, emotionally and spiritually. As one gets into the habit of reading, one gets mental (1)________. It helps us acquire (2)________ and attain intellectual (3)_________. Reading takes away our (4)_________. Reading can bring (5)__________ in our sorrowful times and guide us in our duties.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. comfort.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Reading "can bring comfort in our sorrowful times" — it provides solace and consolation when we are sad. This matches the emotional benefit mentioned earlier. (सांत्वना / आराम)

◦ Correct: Reading can bring comfort in our sorrowful times and guide us in our duties.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "resentment" (bitterness), Option 3 "lethargy" (laziness) and Option 4 "oppression" (cruel treatment) all carry negative meanings that clash with "sorrowful times".

NOTE

• Synonyms of comfort: solace, consolation, relief, reassurance. In sad times we seek comfort, not resentment or oppression.

question: Who among the following was awarded the Sansad Ratna Award 2023 and represents the Indian National Congress in Lok Sabha from West Bengal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury, a Member of Parliament of the Indian National Congress from Baharampur (Berhampore), West Bengal, was among the recipients of the Sansad Ratna Award 2023. (अधीर रंजन चौधरी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Sansad Ratna Award honours top-performing Members of Parliament based on their participation in debates, private member bills and questions raised.

• The award was instituted in 2010, inspired by the vision of former President Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam.

NOTE

• Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury served as the leader of the Congress in the 17th Lok Sabha and as West Bengal Congress president.

question: Where is the Kala Ghoda Arts Festival organised every year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mumbai.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Kala Ghoda Arts Festival is a famous annual cultural festival held in the Kala Ghoda art district of South Mumbai (Maharashtra). (काला घोड़ा कला महोत्सव — मुंबई)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• It is a nine-day festival, usually held in February, showcasing art, music, dance, theatre, cinema, literature and workshops.

• "Kala Ghoda" means "Black Horse", named after a former equestrian statue of King Edward VII in the area.

NOTE

• Other well-known cultural festivals: Surajkund Mela (Haryana), Hornbill Festival (Nagaland), Konark Dance Festival (Odisha).

question: Who wrote the novel ‘Amrit Aur Vish’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amritlal Nagar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Hindi novel "Amrit Aur Vish" (अमृत और विष) was written by the renowned Hindi writer Amritlal Nagar. It won him the Sahitya Akademi Award (1985). (अमृतलाल नागर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Amritlal Nagar was a leading figure of modern Hindi literature; his other notable works include Boond Aur Samudra, Manas Ka Hans and Nachyo Bahut Gopal.

NOTE

• Other authors listed: Vishnu Prabhakar (Awara Masiha), Shreelal Shukla (Raag Darbari) and Ramdhari Singh Dinkar (Rashmirathi, Urvashi).

question: Who inaugurated 'Vibrant Village Program' in april 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amit Shah.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Vibrant Villages Programme was inaugurated/launched by Union Home Minister Amit Shah in April 2023 from Kibithoo village in Arunachal Pradesh. (गृह मंत्री अमित शाह)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The programme aims at the comprehensive development of villages along the northern (India–China) border to improve infrastructure, connectivity and livelihood and to check out-migration.

• It covers border villages in Arunachal Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Sikkim, Uttarakhand and Ladakh.

NOTE

• The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Home Affairs and helps transform border villages into "vibrant" and well-connected settlements.

question: The ‘Dhansiri’ and ‘Subansiri’ are the tributaries of ________ River.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Brahmaputra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Dhansiri" and "Subansiri" rivers are important tributaries of the Brahmaputra River, flowing largely through Assam and Arunachal Pradesh. (ब्रह्मपुत्र नदी की सहायक नदियाँ)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Subansiri ("Gold River") is the largest tributary of the Brahmaputra.

• Other left-bank tributaries of the Brahmaputra include the Lohit, Dibang, Kameng and Manas.

NOTE

• The Brahmaputra rises in Tibet (as the Tsangpo), enters India in Arunachal Pradesh (as Siang/Dihang) and flows through Assam before entering Bangladesh (as Jamuna).

question: Why are wealth taxes and gift taxes treated as paper taxes in India?
option_1: It is not mandatory for the government to collect these taxes.
option_2: They do not generate much revenue in comparison to others.
option_3: Tax payers need to fill out forms only in paper and submit returns.
option_4: They are paid only by government employees, members of the Parliament and Legislative assemblies.
solution_text:
The correct answer is They do not generate much revenue in comparison to others.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Wealth tax and gift tax are called "paper taxes" because they do not generate much revenue for the government compared to other taxes (like income tax and GST) — they exist largely on paper but yield very little collection. (कागज़ी कर — बहुत कम राजस्व)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• A "paper tax" is a tax whose contribution to total tax revenue is negligible.

• Wealth Tax in India was abolished in 2015 (Union Budget 2015–16) because its collection cost was high relative to the low revenue it earned.

NOTE

• Taxes are of two types: direct taxes (income tax, corporate tax — paid directly) and indirect taxes (GST, customs — paid on goods/services).

question: What is the primary role of autotrophic organisms in an ecosystem?
option_2: Producing organic matter from inorganic substances
option_3: Preying on other organisms for food
solution_text:
The correct answer is Producing organic matter from inorganic substances.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Autotrophs (like green plants and algae) are the producers of an ecosystem — they produce organic matter (food) from inorganic substances (CO₂ and water) using sunlight through photosynthesis. (स्वपोषी — उत्पादक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Autotrophs form the base of the food chain and capture solar energy, making it available to the rest of the ecosystem.

• Breaking down dead organisms = role of decomposers (bacteria, fungi); preying on others = consumers/heterotrophs.

NOTE

• Ecosystem components: Producers (autotrophs), Consumers (herbivores, carnivores) and Decomposers. Photosynthesis: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂.

question: Which of the following water bodies are also known as nurseries of the ocean?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Estuaries.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Estuaries — where a river meets the sea and fresh water mixes with salt water — are called the "nurseries of the ocean" because they are rich in nutrients and provide breeding and feeding grounds for many fish and other marine species. (ज्वारनदमुख — महासागर की नर्सरी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Estuaries support high biodiversity and are among the most productive ecosystems on Earth.

• Examples in India: the estuaries of the Ganga, Godavari, Krishna and Narmada rivers.

NOTE

• A lagoon is a shallow water body separated from the sea by a sandbar (e.g., Chilika Lake); a bog is a type of wetland with acidic, spongy ground.

question: Identify the Kuchipudi dancer, actor and film producer who won the best choreography award at the 68th National Film Awards 2022.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sandhya Raju.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sandhya Raju, a Kuchipudi dancer, actor and film producer, won the Best Choreography award at the 68th National Film Awards (2022) for the film Natyam. (संध्या राजू — कुचिपुड़ी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Kuchipudi is a classical dance form of Andhra Pradesh.

• The National Film Awards are presented by the Directorate of Film Festivals under the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.

NOTE

• The legendary Birju Maharaj was a Kathak maestro (also an occasional film choreographer); Ganesh Acharya and Remo D'Souza are noted Bollywood choreographers.

question: Tanras Khan is associated with which of the following gharanas?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Delhi gharana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Tanras Khan was a famous vocalist associated with the "Delhi gharana" of Hindustani classical music. He was a court musician of the last Mughal emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar. (दिल्ली घराना)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Delhi gharana is regarded as one of the oldest gharanas of khyal singing in Hindustani classical music.

• A "gharana" is a system/lineage of musical training that shares a distinctive style and traces to a particular place or founder.

NOTE

• Some khyal gharanas: Gwalior, Agra, Kirana, Patiala, Jaipur-Atrauli and Delhi. The Gwalior gharana is considered the oldest khyal gharana.

question: According to the standard definition of Census of India, the marginal worker is a person who works for less than _______ days in a year.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 183.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Census of India, a "marginal worker" is a person who worked for less than 183 days (i.e., less than six months) in a year. (सीमांत श्रमिक — 183 दिन से कम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• A "main worker" is one who worked for 183 days or more (six months or more) in a year.

• Workers are classified into main workers and marginal workers based on the duration of work.

NOTE

• The Census of India is conducted every 10 years (decennial); the first synchronous census was in 1881 under Lord Ripon. The Census organisation works under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

question: The Banaras session of the Indian National Congress in 1905 was presided over by _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gopal Krishna Gokhale.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Banaras (Varanasi) session of the Indian National Congress in 1905 was presided over by Gopal Krishna Gokhale. (गोपाल कृष्ण गोखले — बनारस अधिवेशन 1905)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The 1905 session took place against the backdrop of the Partition of Bengal (1905) and the rise of the Swadeshi Movement.

• Gopal Krishna Gokhale was a moderate leader and the political mentor (guru) of Mahatma Gandhi; he founded the Servants of India Society (1905).

NOTE

• The first session of the INC (1885, Bombay) was presided over by W. C. Bonnerjee. The INC was founded by A. O. Hume.

question: The ‘Agaria’ community of the 19th century was associated with which of the following industries?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Iron industry.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Agaria" community was a group of traditional iron smelters/iron workers associated with the iron industry (iron smelting) in central India during the 19th century. (अगरिया — लौह उद्योग)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Agarias were skilled in smelting iron ore using traditional furnaces and were prominent in regions of present-day Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh.

• Their craft declined with the advent of imported iron and industrial-scale steel production during British rule.

NOTE

• The word "Agaria" is linked to the traditional occupation of iron making; other artisan communities declined similarly under colonial industrialisation.

question: Pushyamitra Sunga's capital was at:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pataliputra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pushyamitra Sunga, the founder of the Sunga dynasty, had his capital at Pataliputra (modern Patna, Bihar). (पुष्यमित्र शुंग — पाटलिपुत्र)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Pushyamitra Sunga founded the Sunga dynasty around 185 BCE after overthrowing the last Mauryan ruler Brihadratha.

• He is known for performing the Ashvamedha (horse) sacrifice and for the patronage of Brahmanism; Patanjali was associated with his court.

NOTE

• Pataliputra was the capital of the Magadha empire under the Nandas, Mauryas and Sungas. It was founded by Ajatashatru/Udayin of the Haryanka dynasty.

question: What is the charge of an electron?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Negative.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An electron carries a negative electric charge of −1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ coulombs. (इलेक्ट्रॉन — ऋणात्मक आवेश)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The proton carries an equal positive charge (+1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C), and the neutron is electrically neutral.

• The electron was discovered by J. J. Thomson in 1897.

NOTE

• Sub-atomic particles: electron (negative, in shells), proton (positive, in nucleus), neutron (neutral, in nucleus). Mass of electron ≈ 9.1 × 10⁻³¹ kg (about 1/1836 of a proton).

question: Excessive bleeding from wounds may happen due to lack of ____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vitamin K.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting (coagulation). Its deficiency leads to excessive bleeding from wounds because the blood cannot clot properly. (विटामिन K — रक्त का थक्का जमना)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Vitamin K helps the liver synthesise prothrombin, a protein needed for clotting.

• Its chemical name is phylloquinone (K1); good sources are green leafy vegetables, cabbage and broccoli.

NOTE

• Fat-soluble vitamins: A, D, E, K. Vitamin A → vision, Vitamin D → bones, Vitamin E → antioxidant/fertility, Vitamin K → clotting.

question: What is the term for a dome-shaped monument that contains sacred relics in Buddhism?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Stupa.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Stupa" is a dome-shaped (hemispherical) Buddhist monument built to enshrine sacred relics of the Buddha or Buddhist monks and used for meditation and worship. (स्तूप)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Sanchi Stupa (Madhya Pradesh), originally built by Emperor Ashoka, is the most famous stupa in India and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

• Parts of a stupa: the anda (dome), harmika, yashti (mast) and chhatra (umbrella).

NOTE

• Other Buddhist architecture: Vihara (a monastery/residence for monks), Chaitya (a prayer hall), Stambha (a pillar, e.g., Ashokan pillars).

question: In which of the following cases did the Supreme Court of India propound the Basic Structure Doctrine of the Constitution?
option_1: Kesavanad Bharati vs. State of Kerala Case
option_2: Maneka Gandhi vs Union of India Case
option_3: Golakhnath vs. State of Punjab Case
option_4: Indira Gandhi vs. Raj Narayan Case
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kesavanad Bharati vs. State of Kerala Case.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Basic Structure Doctrine was propounded by the Supreme Court in the landmark Kesavananda Bharati vs. State of Kerala case (1973). It held that Parliament can amend the Constitution but cannot alter its "basic structure". (केशवानंद भारती वाद, 1973)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The case was decided by a 13-judge bench (the largest ever), by a 7–6 majority.

• Elements of the basic structure include the supremacy of the Constitution, rule of law, separation of powers, judicial review, secularism and federalism.

NOTE

• Golaknath case (1967) held that Parliament cannot amend Fundamental Rights; Maneka Gandhi case (1978) expanded Article 21 (right to life and personal liberty).

question: Anahat Singh is associated with which of the following sports events?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Squash.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Anahat Singh is a young Indian squash player who has won several national and international titles, including a gold medal at the 2022 Commonwealth Games (mixed doubles/junior events) and success at the Asian Games. (अनाहत सिंह — स्क्वैश)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Squash is a racquet sport played in a four-walled court with a small hollow rubber ball.

• Anahat Singh is regarded as one of India's brightest young squash prospects.

NOTE

• India's notable squash players: Saurav Ghosal, Dipika Pallikal, Joshna Chinappa and Anahat Singh.

question: Fugdi is famous dance of the state of _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Goa.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Fugdi" is a traditional folk dance of Goa (also popular in the Konkan region of Maharashtra), performed by women during Hindu festivals like Ganesh Chaturthi and Vrata. (फुगड़ी — गोवा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• In Fugdi, women dance in a circle or rows, often clapping and singing, at a gradually increasing pace.

• Other folk dances of Goa: Dekhni, Dhalo, Ghode Modni, Corridinho and Fugdi.

NOTE

• Folk dances: Punjab – Bhangra/Giddha; Tamil Nadu – Karagattam/Kummi; Uttarakhand – Chholiya; Goa – Fugdi/Dekhni.

question: The Border-Gavaskar trophy is played between _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is India and Australia.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Border–Gavaskar Trophy" is a Test cricket series contested between India and Australia. (बॉर्डर-गावस्कर ट्रॉफी — भारत और ऑस्ट्रेलिया)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The trophy is named after two legendary cricketers — Allan Border (Australia) and Sunil Gavaskar (India).

• It was instituted in 1996–97.

NOTE

• Other bilateral Test trophies: The Ashes (England vs Australia), Frank Worrell Trophy (Australia vs West Indies), Pataudi Trophy (India vs England, in England).

question: Which of the following reports is considered as a piecemeal effort to provide resilience to the successful working of federal system?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sarkaria Commission.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Sarkaria Commission report is regarded as an effort to strengthen and provide resilience to the federal system by reviewing Centre–State relations in India. (सरकारिया आयोग — केंद्र-राज्य संबंध)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Sarkaria Commission was set up in 1983 under Justice R. S. Sarkaria and submitted its report in 1988, recommending measures to improve Centre–State relations (e.g., on the role of the Governor and Article 356).

• Later, the Punchhi Commission (2007) further examined Centre–State relations.

NOTE

• Kothari Commission (1964–66) dealt with education; commissions of inquiry like Thakkar and Kapur were set up to investigate specific incidents.

question: In 1527, Babur defeated Rana Sanga, the Rajput ruler of Mewar in the Battle of ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Khanwa.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In 1527, Babur defeated Rana Sanga (Rana Sangram Singh), the Rajput ruler of Mewar, in the Battle of Khanwa (near Fatehpur Sikri, Rajasthan). (खानवा का युद्ध, 1527)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Babur used superior artillery and the tulughma war tactics to win, strengthening the newly founded Mughal Empire.

• After this victory, Babur assumed the title "Ghazi".

NOTE

• Babur's major battles: First Battle of Panipat (1526) against Ibrahim Lodi; Khanwa (1527) against Rana Sanga; Chanderi (1528) against Medini Rai; Ghaghra (1529) against the Afghans.

question: According to the Multidimensional Poverty Index 2023, which union territory has the least percentage of poor?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Puducherry.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) 2023 (NITI Aayog), among the union territories, Puducherry had the least percentage of multidimensionally poor people. (बहुआयामी गरीबी सूचकांक 2023 — पुदुचेरी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• India's National MPI is prepared by NITI Aayog, based on the methodology of the UNDP and OPHI (Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative).

• It measures deprivation across three dimensions — Health, Education and Standard of Living — using 12 indicators.

NOTE

• The MPI report noted that a large number of Indians escaped multidimensional poverty between 2015–16 and 2019–21.

question: The North-South National Highway Corridor connects which two UTs/States of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jammu and Kashmir - Tamil Nadu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The North–South Corridor of the National Highways connects Srinagar (Jammu and Kashmir) in the north to Kanyakumari (Tamil Nadu) in the south. (उत्तर-दक्षिण गलियारा — जम्मू-कश्मीर से तमिलनाडु)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The North–South and East–West Corridors are part of the National Highways Development Project (NHDP) of the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI).

• The East–West Corridor connects Silchar (Assam) to Porbandar (Gujarat).

NOTE

• The Golden Quadrilateral connects the four metros — Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata — and is India's largest highway project.
